obernants.operator: In the universe of input pairs and candidate Result vectors, absent successful behavior includes wrong output length, noncanonical residues, or any coefficient unequal to sum a[i]*b[t-i] modulo p. Errors follow empty/length/cap/allocation order. This target is a specification, not a semantic proof.

obernants.operator: The preimage of output y contains all admissible ordered factor pairs whose finite-field polynomial product equals y and whose explicit lengths yield y.len, plus empty-input pairs for empty y. Factor swapping, scalar units and residue lifts cause ambiguity; [2]*[3] and [1]*[6] coincide.

obernants.operator: For fixed power-of-two L<=2^23 and canonical field vectors, inverse(forward(v))=v because the chosen root has exact order L and L is nonzero in the field. Unique recovery applies to the full padded transform vector, not the convolution factor pair.

obernants.operator: p=998244353 is prime and p-1=119*2^23. Trial division through floor(sqrt(p)) checks primality; testing 3^((p-1)/q)!=1 for q=2,7,17 verifies primitive order. Therefore 3^((p-1)/L) has order L for every supported L. Tests check all 24 lengths algebraically, not by allocating maximal arrays.

obernants.operator: For every field point z, eval(convolution(a,b),z)=eval(a,z)*eval(b,z). At z=1 this becomes coefficient-mass multiplication. Finite point evaluation complements independent schoolbook checks but alone is incomplete.

obernants.operator: Input coefficients reduce modulo p before butterflies. Residues remain below p; butterfly sums are below2p and products below p^2<2^60, safely inside u64. Inverse scaling is n^(p-2). Arbitrary u64 input cannot overflow a product before normalization.

obernants.operator: Empty operands return empty before length arithmetic. Otherwise checked a+(b-1), checked next power of two, and L<=2^23 precede allocation. Two L-word buffers dominate space; allocation refusal is reported. Arithmetic/cap tests use the private lengths helper to avoid oversized allocations.
